inputs.source: On-call engineer's chat request, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: The agent will deploy or migrate 'the named service' in production whenever asked, with no stated restriction on which services or migrations, and no check that the request is appropriate.
Explicit instruction to never ask for confirmation before irreversible production actions removes any human-in-the-loop safeguard, justified only by the engineer being busy.

elements.name: Chat request channel from engineer to agent

controls.name: SSO-authenticated access restricted to on-call engineers
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the identity provider outside the model; establishes that only an authenticated on-call engineer can reach the agent at all (why the input is classed trusted, not untrusted). It does not constrain what an authenticated engineer can ask the agent to do, so it earns no credit against the findings in this assessment.

controls.name: Cloud audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the cloud platform outside the model and does not weaken with model capability, but it records every action under the engineer's identity without distinguishing agent-initiated from manual actions, so it does not establish agent accountability and earns no tier credit (detective only).

controls.name: Human approval gate before irreversible or production actions
Rate or step limit on production deploy/migrate actions
Tamper-evident, non-deletable record of requests and rationale

findings.title: Trusted request directly triggers an irreversible, unreviewed production migration

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated on-call engineer asks the agent to run a named migration.
Agent runs the migration immediately in production using the engineer's own token, with no confirmation step and no automatic rollback.

threat_refs.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Watch for removal of the SSO/on-call restriction, expansion of who can message the agent, or the agent being issued its own broader service credential instead of the requester's own token.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to run the named migration in production using the engineer's credentials whenever asked, and explicitly forbids asking for confirmation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, and the agent uses the engineer's personal access token, passed in at session start, for every production action.

recommendations.action: Require a raw-action human approval gate, reviewed individually, before executing any production database migration.
Automate a pre-migration snapshot or backup so migrations are no longer unilaterally irreversible.

findings.title: Trusted request directly triggers an unreviewed production deployment

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated on-call engineer asks the agent to deploy a named service.
Agent deploys immediately in production using the engineer's own token, with no confirmation step.

forecast.watch_signal: Watch for new deployment tooling that removes rollback capability, or for the deploy credential scope widening beyond the requesting engineer's own access; either would be reassessed against a higher sink class.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to deploy the named service in production using the engineer's credentials whenever asked, without confirmation.
The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token, passed in at session start.

recommendations.action: Require approval or a staged/canary rollout confirmation before production deploys.

findings.title: No attributable record separates agent-initiated production actions from the engineer's own actions, and the only record of intent is deletable

forecast.watch_signal: Watch for the agent being granted its own distinct service identity without a corresponding provenance mechanism, or for chat retention policy changes that still allow user-initiated deletion.

evidence.observation: The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript. Engineers can delete their own chat history.
Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, not distinguished from the engineer's own manual actions.

recommendations.action: Generate tamper-evident, agent-attributed action records (distinct from the engineer's identity) for every production action, including the originating request, stored where the requesting engineer cannot delete it.
Make the record of requests and agent rationale immutable or retained independent of user-initiated deletion of the chat transcript.

findings.title: No step, rate, or spend limit bounds repeated production deploy or migration actions

forecast.watch_signal: Watch for the agent being used for batch, scheduled, or multi-step operations, or for max_unattended_steps/max_runtime remaining unset as usage grows.

evidence.observation: No mention of a limit on how many deploys or migrations may be requested or run in a session.
No spend, rate, or step limit is described anywhere in the runtime configuration.

recommendations.action: Add a rate or step limit on production deploy and migration actions per session or time window.

stride_coverage.rationale: No peer agents, MCP servers, or external processes interact with deploy-assistant as a client; only the SSO-authenticated engineer invokes it directly, so there is no process identity for another entity to spoof.
The agent cannot modify its own configuration or prompt (can_modify_own_config is false) and no mechanism for external parties to alter its logic is described.
The agent has no egress capability and responds only to the authenticated requesting engineer, so there is no channel for disclosing data outside the interaction.

The agent acts only with the requesting engineer's own personal access token and never holds broader privilege than that engineer already has, so it cannot escalate privilege beyond the requester's own access.
Artifacts do not describe access controls, retention, or encryption for the chat transcript store, so disclosure risk to other parties cannot be assessed from the design documents provided.
Chat history storage has no described effect on the availability of deploy or migrate actions; exhausting it would not block production capabilities.
Artifacts do not state whether the cloud audit log is immutable, who can modify or purge entries, or how long it is retained.
Artifacts do not describe access controls on who can read the cloud audit log, so disclosure risk cannot be assessed.
Artifacts do not describe logging capacity, retention limits, or failure behavior of the cloud audit log under load.
Artifacts do not describe what data the migration touches or who could read it; disclosure risk from the migration itself is not assessed here.
Availability impact from a single faulty migration is captured as a consequence of find.db_migrate_no_confirmation rather than a distinct service-disruption technique.
Deploying a service does not itself read or expose internal data beyond what the service already serves; no new disclosure pathway is introduced by the deploy action.
Availability impact from a single deploy action is captured as a consequence of find.prod_deploy_no_confirmation rather than a distinct denial-of-service technique.

rating.rationale: Every production-affecting path in this design starts from a trusted, SSO-authenticated engineer, so no untrusted-source lethal-trifecta pattern applies; risk instead comes from the rubric's trusted-to-severe-sink cell (a trusted principal can still direct an irreversible action by accident) combined with an autonomy modifier, since no step or runtime limit is declared. The migration path and both property findings (missing attributable provenance; no rate/step limit) compute to high; the deploy path computes to moderate. No credited control reduces any of these: the only declared controls are SSO access scoping (which justifies the trusted classification but does not constrain what a trusted requester can direct) and a cloud audit log (detective, and itself part of the repudiation problem because it attributes every action to the engineer's identity without distinguishing agent action from manual action). Because there are no dependent or partially-dependent controls in place today, no trigger causes further control decay; forecast equals residual for three of four findings. The single missing control most responsible for the residual ceiling is the human approval gate on irreversible production actions (control.require_confirmation, status missing_recommended) plus its companion control for distinguishing agent-attributed action records (control.agent_identity_tagging).

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; capability scope (exact migration/deploy tooling, blast radius) is inferred from the prompt and runtime notes.

The immutability, retention, and access controls of the cloud audit log and the chat history store are not described; whether either can itself be altered, purged, or read by unauthorized parties is unknown.

No information was provided on whether the on-call roster, SSO session, or personal access tokens have additional compensating controls (for example, token scope limits or session timeouts) beyond what is stated.
